info.title: graphersal-server HTTP API (EXPERIMENTAL)
info.summary: The server's own routes: login, the caller's databases and the admin API.
info.description:
**EXPERIMENTAL.** The HTTP API of graphersal-server itself: the probes, the browser login, the caller's databases and the admin API below `/api/admin/` (admins only). `info.version` is the server's version.

**The databases.** Each database (or alias) `<name>` serves its own HTTP API below `/db/<name>/` (queries, schema, saved queries, indexes, jobs, Store, ...), described by its own document at `GET /db/<name>/openapi.json` (`/api/info` names the path template as `databaseOpenapi`, `GET /api/databases` the path of each database as `openapi`); generate a client from that one for data access.

**MCP.** `/mcp` (every database the caller may see) and `/db/<name>/mcp` (one database) are MCP endpoints (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC), not REST routes: point an MCP client at them with the same Bearer token. `404` when `server.toml [mcp] enabled = false`, `503` while `mcp.toml` switches MCP off. See the repository's book, `book/src/guide/mcp.md`.

**Security.** Send a user token as `Authorization: Bearer <64 hex digits>` (`bearerAuth`); a browser uses the `gs_session` cookie set by `POST /api/login` (`sessionCookie`). Wrong credentials are `401`, never anonymous. The admin API needs the admin role: anonymous gets `401`, a user without the role `404` as if the API did not exist. With `server.toml [access] enabled = false` every request runs as the admin `everyone`.

**Every request** but the probes is checked by `Host` (the listen address's names and `server.toml [http] allowed_hosts`) and `Origin` (a browser page of another origin): `403`. While the server starts or stops it answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1`.

**Conventions.** Request bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`, at most 16 MiB; unknown fields `400`), except the uploads of import and models. An error is `{"error", "help"?}`. Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. Shared objects carry a `revision` (users and grants, aliases, each database's settings, the MCP settings): a change may name the revision it was based on (the body's `revision`, else `If-Match: "<revision>"`) and is refused with `409 {error, help, revision}` when someone else changed the object since; nothing changes. Every `GET` but the downloads also answers `HEAD`. The admin actions take real database names; names are case-insensitive. The repository's book (`book/src/reference/admin_api.md`) documents every answer in full; this description is deliberately looser.

get.description: Always `200 {"status": "ok"}` while the process answers. No `Host`/`Origin` check (a probe names the pod IP), no credentials.
`200 {"status": "ready"}` once the server serves requests, `503 {"status": "loading" | "stopping"}` before and while it stops. No `Host`/`Origin` check, no credentials.

The server's own OpenAPI description (this document), `servers` set to the URL the request came to (`server.toml [http] public_scheme` and the request's `Host`). Public: it carries no data. `graphersal-server openapi --dir DIR` writes the same file offline.

The OpenAPI description of the database's own HTTP API (the engine's: queries, schema, saved queries, indexes, jobs, Store, ...), with `servers` = `<this server>/db/<name>`, the same security schemes as this document, and the access layer's answers (401, 404, 409) on every operation; every writing operation carries `x-graphersal-access: write`. `<name>` may be an alias. Needs at least a read grant on the name (anonymous: an anonymous grant), like every route below `/db/<name>/`; answered also while the database is not loaded. `graphersal-server openapi --dir DIR --db NAME` writes the same file offline. Also at `/db/{name}/api/openapi.json`.

post.description: Starts a browser session for a user token: the answer sets the cookie `gs_session` (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, `Max-Age` = `[sessions] lifetime_secs`, else 400 days; `Secure` with `public_scheme = "https"`). Clients that are not browsers send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead and never need this. Runs before authentication: a stale cookie does not block it.
Ends the browser session of the request's `gs_session` cookie (if any) and clears the cookie (`Max-Age=0`). `loggedOut: false`: there was no live session.

post.summary: Reset a layer: discard its changes
post.description: Discards every change of the layer database `{name}` over its base; the base and other layers are untouched. A new empty layer over the same base takes the old one's place, the old layer Store moves to `trash/<name>-<UTC time>/` (recoverable by hand). Kept: name, base, description, read-only and auto-load flags, query limit overrides, grants (also via aliases), aliases, MCP settings and the layer's scheduled job definitions. Discarded: data changes, the layer's own schema and other catalog changes, its history. A loaded layer is unloaded and loaded again (`reloaded`). Needs `confirm: true`. `409` for a plain, base or failed database.

200.description: The server settings after the change, with `changed`, `applied` and `rewritten`.

post.description: `202`, then the server stops as on SIGTERM. The operator or an admin user only (`everyone` of a server without access control: `403`); a server without a stop hook: `409`.

403.description: The principal `everyone`, or a refused Host/Origin.

bearerAuth.description: A user token: 64 hex digits (256 random bits), shown once by `graphersal-server user add` / `user token` or the admin API. The console's operator token (`server.run`) works the same.

sessionCookie.name: gs_session
sessionCookie.description: The browser session cookie `POST /api/login` sets (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict).

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: `"<revision>"`: the revision the change is based on, when the body has no `revision` (`*` checks nothing). Stale: `409`.

BadRequest.description: An invalid name, body, query or schema.

Unauthorized.description: No credentials (`{"error", "login": "/"}`, `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`), or a token nobody holds.

BadCredentials.description: A token nobody holds, or an ended session cookie (cleared with the answer). Never answered as anonymous.

AdminNotFound.description: No such database, alias, user, model or backup; or the caller is logged in without the admin role (the admin API does not exist for it).

DatabaseUnauthorized.description: Anonymous without a grant on the name: `401` for EVERY name (nothing about existence leaks).

DatabaseNotFound.description: No such database or alias, or one the caller has no grant on (it does not exist for the caller).

NotAllowed.description: The method is not allowed on this path.

RevisionConflict.description: Changed by someone else since the given revision (`help: "changed by someone else: reload"`, `revision`: the current one); nothing changed. Or another rule refuses it.

Refused.description: A rule refuses it (name taken, loaded, named by an alias, base of layers, offline, a failed database, ...); `help` says what to do.

TooLarge.description: The body is larger than allowed.

Unsupported.description: An import source of no known format, or a JSON body without `Content-Type: application/json`.

HostRefused.description: A `Host` the server does not answer to, or an `Origin` of another site.

Failure.description: A Store or file operation failed.

Unavailable.description: The server is starting or stopping; retry (`Retry-After: 1`).

error.description: What went wrong, in one sentence.

databaseOpenapi.description: The path template of a database's description: `/db/{name}/openapi.json`.

name.description: The database's name (an alias row: the alias).

revision.description: Of its `database.toml`: send it with a settings change.

leftoverGrantsRemoved.description: Grants left on a NEW name, removed first (absent when none).

Entry.description: One database (listing rows and most actions' answers); see `book/src/reference/admin_api.md` "Entry".

serverDefaults.description: What a new database starts with: `autoLoad`, `readOnly`, `chunkBytes`, `damagePolicy` (`server.toml [defaults]`), `mcpExposeNew` (`mcp.toml`); or `{error}`.

backup.description: Its name (the UTC time with dashes): what restore takes.

database.description: A real name, an alias, or `*`.

restartPending.description: The `server.toml` keys whose change waits for a restart (round 4).

ServerSettings.description: `server.toml` as the admin API shows it (round 4).
